record.body:
This Signature model designs an ocean soundscape as a depth-layered system. Surface wave geophony is specified by a wave-period parameter, reef-like virtual shrimp add broadband crackle in shallow bands, virtual whale-like singers add long low-frequency phrases, and a deep sound channel parameter carries low-frequency energy over a stated distance. The model computes travel times in water, compares them with travel times in air, and reports which voices dominate each depth band. No ocean is recorded and no real whale is imitated as a field claim: the model is arithmetic and scheduling, and any rendered ocean sound is labelled SIMULATED. Its purpose is teaching why the ocean is a long-distance acoustic world and giving sound designers a deep-water template.

Science proof

Science proof: the model encodes the published physics of ocean sound: faster sound in water than in air, long low-frequency range, and the deep sound channel's trapping effect. Those are measured features of ocean acoustics, and the model states its speed and distance parameters so its travel-time figures can be checked by hand.

Math proof

Math proof: sound in seawater travels at roughly 1500 metres per second, about 1500 / 343 = 4.37 times the speed in air. A sound crossing 75 kilometres takes 75000 / 1500 = 50.0 seconds in water and 75000 / 343 = 218.7 seconds in air. The demo prints the ratio 4.37, water time 50.0 seconds, and air time 218.7 seconds.

Soundscape layer(s)

biophony; geophony

Source

Signature design study for this database, October 2026; ocean acoustics as in the public edition

demo.code:
v_water, v_air = 1500.0, 343.0
print('Speed ratio water to air: %.2f' % (v_water / v_air))
print('Water travel time over 75 km: %.1f seconds' % (75000 / v_water))
print('Air travel time over 75 km: %.1f seconds' % (75000 / v_air))
demo.expected_output:
Speed ratio water to air: 4.37
Water travel time over 75 km: 50.0 seconds
Air travel time over 75 km: 218.7 seconds
